question: Will the official price band for the NSE IPO be announced on or before September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo (no band) is only ~10 days from being overturned, but every gating item has cleared: SC disposed the co-location appeals 3 Sep, SEBI issued the observation letter 4 Sep, the settlement was paid, 20 bankers are mandated, and Bloomberg reports the global roadshow is essentially complete — issuers finish roadshows immediately before the anchor book and band advertisement. Reference-class anchor before news: Indian IPOs with a banker-sourced price-band date reported ~1 week out land the official band within a week of that date roughly three times in four; here the question grants ~6 extra days beyond the reported 11 Sep target. SEBI ICDR's two-working-day rule means any open date through Mon 21 Sep forces the band on or before Thu 17 Sep, and the widely reported 25 Sep listing target requires an even earlier band. Adjusting down for: reported open dates already drifting 15→18→21 Sep within three days; one credible outlet (Deccan Chronicle, 5 Sep) placing NSE in the Oct–Nov window instead; NSE's decade-long history of slippage; and 14 Sep being a market holiday, leaving only four working days after 11 Sep. No prediction market prices this. The dominant NO path is a decision to skip Pitru Paksha entirely and relaunch mid-October.

Settled from the ICDR T-2-working-day rule and the shared calendar (Sept 14 Ganesh Chaturthi holiday, Sept 19-20 weekend): announce Fri 18 -> +2 working days = Tue 22, so Runs 1/2 are correct and Run 3 contradicts itself two lines later. The true forcing line is open <= Mon Sept 21. (2) Whether the RHP has been filed with the RoC: all three searched and none could confirm it; no web access on this run, so it stays UNSETTLED and is priced as live uncertainty, not resolved by fiat. (3) Deccan Chronicle's Sept 5 placement of NSE in an Oct-Nov window, surfaced only by Run 1, could not be checked; I downweighted it as one seasonal-preview piece against Reuters, CNBC-TV18, BusinessToday and Sept-7-updated trackers all clustering mid-September, and as apparently not reflecting the Sept 4 observation letter or the ~Sept 6 roadshow-completion reporting — but I left the October branch ~12% rather than closing it. Decomposing over open date (<=Sept 21 ~0.75 -> YES; Sept 22-23 ~0.13 at ~0.45 YES since Indian practice often beats the T-2 floor; punt ~0.12 -> NO) gives ~0.84, reached independently of the runs' numbers.
